Q: Bash wrongly resolves $USERPROFILE for docker volume A:

It isn't $USERPROFILE. It's Git Bash rewriting your /https/... arguments into Windows paths before Docker ever sees them.

Look at the path in your error: C:/Program Files/Git/https/aspnetapp.pfx. That prefix is the MSYS root of a standard Git for Windows install. MSYS sees an argument starting with a single /, assumes it's meant to be a Windows path, and expands it to the install root. Your .bat version works because cmd doesn't do this.

Two of your arguments get mangled:

-e ASPNETCORE_Kestrel__Certificates__Default__Path=/https/aspnetapp.pfx
-v "$USERPROFILE/.aspnet/https:/https/"

The env var is the one producing your error. It arrives inside the container as C:/Program Files/Git/https/aspnetapp.pfx, which isn't an absolute path there, so Kestrel resolves it against the working directory and you get /app/C:/Program Files/....

Turn the conversion off for that one command:

MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 docker run --rm -it \
    -p 5001:5001 \
    -e ASPNETCORE_URLS="https://+:5001" \
    ...

A leading // also escapes it if you'd rather not set the variable, but MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 is easier to read.

One more thing: use $HOME rather than $USERPROFILE in Git Bash. $USERPROFILE expands with backslashes, which is a second way for this to go wrong once the path conversion stops hiding it.

Q: How can I reliably scrape the Meta Ads Library for the latest ad launches? A:

Don't scrape the internal GraphQL endpoint. There's a supported one, ads_archive on the Graph API, and it has the exact filter you're describing:

curl -G \
  -d "search_terms='your term'" \
  -d "ad_type=ALL" \
  -d "ad_reached_countries=['DE']" \
  -d "ad_delivery_date_min=2026-09-01" \
  -d "ad_active_status=ACTIVE" \
  -d "access_token=<TOKEN>" \
  "https://graph.facebook.com/<VERSION>/ads_archive"

ad_delivery_date_min is what you want for "as soon as they start running". Poll that instead of the web app.

Read this limit before you build anything on it, because it decides whether the API is any use to you. From the docs: "Ads that did not reach any location in the EU will only return if they are about social issues, elections or politics."

So ad_type=ALL gives you everything for EU-targeted ads. Outside the EU you only get political and issue ads, and there's no supported way to get commercial ones. If you're tracking US commercial launches, the API won't do it, and that's a policy decision rather than a technical gap.

The AdLibrarySearchPaginationQuery endpoint you found is internal and unversioned. The doc_id changes on deploys, the tokens are short-lived, and it's against the ToS. It'll work until it doesn't.

Q: Set authentication type Bearer when curl with .netrc file A:

You can't. .netrc only holds login and password, and curl turns those into Basic. There's no field or flag that makes it emit a Bearer header.

I checked on curl 8.7.1 against a server that logs what arrives:

  • --netrc-file alone sends Authorization: Basic bXl1c2VyOi4uLg==
  • --oauth2-bearer TOKEN sends Authorization: Bearer TOKEN
  • both together still sends Bearer, and the token comes from the flag. The .netrc password is never used for it.

If what you actually want is the credential in a file instead of on the command line, use a curl config file. It can hold a whole header:

# token.conf
header = "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"

curl --config token.conf "http://url/to/service"

chmod 600 it and you get the same benefit as .netrc, nothing in your shell history or process list, and it works for any auth scheme instead of just Basic.

Q: How to get the object created by customElement in a Web Component? A:

Note that as soon as you have access to an instance of your custom element, you can simply use constructor theft to create new instances:

// let's say you have a reference to `<my-grid />` in `el`:
const newEl = new el.constructor;

Q: How can Playwright send the Proxy-Authorization while using Chromium? A:

Chromium ignores credentials embedded in the proxy URL. Pass them as separate fields instead:

proxy={
    "server": "http://127.0.0.1:8000",
    "username": "abcdef",
    "password": "123456",
}

I reproduced this against a local proxy that logs what it receives. With http://abcdef:123456@127.0.0.1:8000 the proxy got no Proxy-Authorization header at all and the page came back empty. With the credentials as separate fields, Chromium got the 407, retried, and sent Proxy-Authorization: Basic ... correctly.

Worth knowing: Chromium never sends the header preemptively — it always takes the 407 challenge first. If your proxy closes the connection instead of returning 407 with a Proxy-Authenticate header, you get the same blank page even when the credentials are right.

Q: Python discount function returns negative value and passes all linters, mypy, bandit and unit tests A:

This isn't the kind of issue those tools were supposed to address:

  • mypy is supposed to check for type errors, but your function doesn't have any type hints, and even if it did, it's fine.
  • Flake8 is largely for code style and pseudo-syntax errors, not correctness.
  • Bandit is for security issues, and returning a negative number isn't a security issue here.

Pylint can sometimes catch correctness errors, but it has no idea that your code is incorrect here; there's no way for it to understand that a function named apply_discount shouldn't allow discounts greater than 1.

Additionally, your unit tests are insufficient. You should try to test everything you guarantee; if you want a guarantee that this function rejects discounts not in [0, 1], you need to test for that. It's tautological, but only testing the happy path only tests the happy path.

Static analysis tools simply cannot catch every kind of bug. Defining and testing the behavior of your program is your responsibility.

Q: 302 redirect after CORS preflight A:

Redirects for requests that require preflight became allowed some time around 2016, apparently because they were never actually prevented. See https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/204 for the discussion, especially this comment and this exception for URLs containing credentials.
